question: What part of the nervous system is primarily targeted and damaged by the poliovirus?

options.A: Sensory neurons in the dorsal root ganglion
options.B: Motor neurons in the anterior horn cells of the spinal cord
options.C: Myelin sheath of peripheral sensory nerves
options.D: White matter tracts in the cerebellum

explanation: The poliovirus specifically targets and destroys motor neurons located in the anterior horn cells of the spinal cord and brainstem, leading to muscle weakness and paralysis. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T15#GNS313_U2_T15_h1)

question: Which age group is primarily and most severely affected by poliomyelitis?

options.B: Young children under five years of age
options.D: Neonates in the first month of life

explanation: Poliomyelitis is a highly infectious disease that primarily targets young children, typically under the age of five. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T15#GNS313_U2_T15_h1)

question: How many distinct serotypes of the poliovirus exist?
explanation: There are three distinct serotypes of the poliovirus: Type 1, Type 2, and Type 3, requiring immunization coverage against all types. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T15#GNS313_U2_T15_h2)

question: What is the primary mode of transmission for the poliovirus?
explanation: The poliovirus spreads primarily via the fecal-oral route through contaminated hands, water, or food in environments with poor sanitation. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T15#GNS313_U2_T15_h2)

question: Which of the following best describes the characteristics of paralysis caused by polio?

options.A: Symmetrical, spastic paralysis with hyperactive reflexes
options.B: Asymmetrical, flaccid paralysis with absent deep tendon reflexes
options.C: Gradual, ascending paralysis accompanied by loss of all skin sensation
options.D: Localized rigidity restricted entirely to the upper extremities

explanation: Polio paralysis is typically acute, asymmetrical, flaccid in nature, and accompanied by diminished or absent deep tendon reflexes while sensory function remains intact. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T15#GNS313_U2_T15_h3)

question: What is bulbar polio characterized by?

options.A: Infection of the cranial nerve nuclei affecting swallowing and breathing
options.B: Exclusive paralysis of the bilateral lower extremities
options.C: Chronic, progressive dementia without motor deficits
options.D: Severe sensory loss in the hands and feet

explanation: Bulbar polio affects the cranial nerve nuclei in the brainstem, compromising vital functions like swallowing, speech, and spontaneous respiration. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T15#GNS313_U2_T15_h3)

question: What percentage of poliovirus infections are estimated to be asymptomatic or subclinical?
explanation: The vast majority of poliovirus infections (about 72%) are asymptomatic, meaning infected individuals show no outward signs of the disease while still shedding the virus. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T15#GNS313_U2_T15_h4)

question: Abortive poliomyelitis is best described as presenting with which of the following?

options.B: Non-specific viral symptoms like fever, fatigue, and sore throat
options.C: Severe respiratory failure requiring mechanical ventilation
options.D: Marked nuchal rigidity and severe meningeal signs

explanation: Abortive poliomyelitis presents as a mild, non-specific viral illness with symptoms such as fever, headache, and sore throat that resolves quickly without paralysis. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T15#GNS313_U2_T15_h4)

question: What is the primary diagnostic specimen required for laboratory confirmation of suspected poliovirus infection?

options.B: A stool specimen collected within 14 days of paralysis onset

explanation: Stool specimens collected within 14 days of the onset of paralysis are the primary diagnostic samples used to isolate and confirm the presence of the poliovirus. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T15#GNS313_U2_T15_h5)

question: Which clinical finding is a nurse most likely to document during a neurological assessment of a child with paralytic polio?

options.A: Hyperactive deep tendon reflexes and muscle rigidity
options.B: Asymmetrical flaccid muscle weakness and absent reflexes
options.C: Complete loss of pain and temperature sensation in limbs
options.D: Symmetrical spastic paralysis of the upper trunk

explanation: Paralytic polio typically presents with asymmetrical flaccid muscle weakness and diminished or absent deep tendon reflexes while sensory pathways remain intact. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T15#GNS313_U2_T15_h5)

question: What is the primary goal of medical management for a patient with established paralytic poliomyelitis?

options.A: To eradicate the virus using broad-spectrum antiviral drugs
options.B: To provide supportive care, pain relief, and prevention of complications
options.C: To surgically repair damaged spinal cord motor neurons
options.D: To stimulate nerve regeneration using high-dose corticosteroids

explanation: Because there is no cure for polio, medical management focuses on supportive care, managing symptoms, and preventing secondary complications. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T15#GNS313_U2_T15_h6)

question: When should physical therapy and rehabilitation typically be initiated for a polio survivor?

options.A: Immediately during the peak acute phase with severe muscle pain
options.B: Only after the patient has achieved complete spontaneous recovery
options.C: As soon as the acute phase subsides to prevent contractures
options.D: Ten years after the initial infection has resolved

explanation: Rehabilitation and physical therapy are initiated as soon as the acute phase subsides to help maintain joint mobility and prevent permanent contractures. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T15#GNS313_U2_T15_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of maintaining the cold chain during vaccine distribution in Nigeria?

options.A: To freeze the vaccines solid so they last indefinitely
options.B: To ensure heat-sensitive vaccines retain their potency and effectiveness
options.C: To prevent the growth of bacteria on the exterior of glass vials
options.D: To speed up the transport of supplies across difficult terrain

explanation: The cold chain is essential to keep heat-sensitive vaccines like OPV and IPV within required temperature ranges so they do not lose their potency. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T15#GNS313_U2_T15_h7)

question: What tool helps Nigerian healthcare workers visually check if an oral polio vaccine has been exposed to excessive heat?

options.A: A digital thermometer probe inserted inside the cap
options.B: The vaccine vial monitor (VVM) printed on the label
options.C: A color-changing chemical strip inside the vaccine carrier
options.D: An expiration date stamp stamped in red ink

explanation: The vaccine vial monitor (VVM) is a label that changes color to indicate whether the vaccine has been exposed to heat that could compromise its potency. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T15#GNS313_U2_T15_h7)

question: What is a core responsibility of a community health nurse regarding acute flaccid paralysis (AFP) surveillance?

options.A: Prescribing broad-spectrum antibiotics to cure the paralysis
options.B: Identifying, investigating, and reporting any suspected AFP case promptly
options.C: Quarantining entire villages upon the identification of a single fever case
options.D: Performing surgical interventions to correct muscle contractures

explanation: Community health nurses must actively identify, investigate, collect specimens for, and report any suspected case of acute flaccid paralysis through surveillance systems. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T15#GNS313_U2_T15_h8)

question: How do community health nurses effectively address vaccine hesitancy in rural Nigerian communities?

options.A: By imposing financial fines on parents who refuse vaccination
options.B: Through grassroots health education and engaging local community leaders
options.C: By withholding other primary healthcare services from non-compliant families
options.D: By administering vaccines covertly without informing the parents

explanation: Nurses address vaccine hesitancy and build trust by conducting health education and collaborating closely with trusted local leaders and community volunteers. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T15#GNS313_U2_T15_h8)
